name: Devasathan
deity: Shiva and Vishnu (with shrines to Ganesha and Brahma)
significance: The principal Brahmin temple of Thailand, founded in Bangkok in 1784 by King Rama I, housing separate shrines for Shiva, Vishnu and Ganesha. It remains the seat of the royal court Brahmins who conduct state Hindu rites.

name: Shree Shree Siddheswari Kalimandir
significance: An old Kali temple in central Dhaka, dated to 1441 and attributed to a founder named Chand Rai, whose central image of the goddess is its chief object of worship. The Siddheshwari neighbourhood of the city takes its name from the shrine.

name: Laxmi Narayan Mandir, Dhaka
significance: A roughly three-century-old two-storeyed temple on Nawabpur Road in old Dhaka dedicated to Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth. It has no dome, carries carved scenes from Hindu mythology and holds marble images brought from Jaipur; it is now run as a private temple with a residence inside its compound.

name: Lalmai Chandi Temple
significance: Also called Chandimura Mandir, this Kali temple crowns the Lalmai hill in Comilla District and is traced to a 7th-century foundation by Rani Probhaboti. It was restored in the 17th century and again in 1972-73, and a Shiva temple stands beside it.

name: Bishyanath Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in Mymensingh district, Bangladesh, noted for its unusual pagoda-like form among the region's Hindu shrines.

name: Boro Kali Bari Temple
builtDisplay: c. 18th c. (reign of Nawab Alivardi Khan)
significance: A Shakta temple in Mymensingh city said to be about three centuries old, founded by Tantric practitioners during the reign of Nawab Alivardi Khan. Its black stone image of Kali was replaced by a new one during a renovation completed in 2026.
story: Temple lore says a fisherman drew a black stone image of Kali from the Brahmaputra in his net and cried out 'Joy Kali!', giving the goddess her name; Tantrics then consecrated the image beneath an old banyan tree.

name: Kal Bhairab Temple, Brahmanbaria
significance: A Shaiva pilgrimage temple at Medda in Brahmanbaria, built about two centuries ago by the sculptor Durgacharan Acharjee on land given by Noor Muhammad, a landlord of Sarail. Its 28-foot image of Kal Bhairab is claimed to be the largest of its kind, and images of Kali and Parvati stand alongside.
story: The sculptor Durgacharan Acharjee is said to have been moved by a dream to shape the great earthen image of Kal Bhairab.

name: Joy Kali Temple
significance: A Kali temple in old Dhaka, reckoned about four centuries old, founded by the Dewans Tulsi Narayan Ghosh and Nabh Narayan Ghosh under the saint Bancharam. It has terracotta-clad walls and columns, a shikhara over the sanctum with mandapa and antarala, and a domed Shiva shrine in the compound.

name: Sugandha Shakta Pitha
significance: One of the Shakta pithas, standing at Shikarpur village about ten miles north of Barisal in Bangladesh, where the goddess is worshipped as Sunanda or Ugratara. Shiva-Chaturdashi is its principal annual festival.
story: The site is held to be where the nose of Sati fell when Vishnu's discus dismembered her body as the grieving Shiva carried it.

name: Muktagachha Shiva Temple
deity: Shiva (as Anandamoyi Shiva), with a paired Kali shrine
significance: Twin Shiva and Kali temples raised in 1820 by Rani Bimola Devi of the Muktagachha zamindar family, named for her mother Anandamoyee. Cited as fine examples of mirrored temple pairs in Bengal, they are a listed heritage site now in fragile condition.
